title: AI Setup (OpenRouter)
headings: AI Setup (OpenRouter) | What you need | Contents | Part 1: Creating an OpenRouter API Key | 1. Create an account | 2. Open the Keys page | 3. Create a new key | 4. Configure the key | 5. Copy your API key | Part 2: Configuring RJ Nexus | 1. Open the AI settings | 2. Paste your API key | 3. Understand the AI settings screen | 4. Fetch and select a model | 5. Check model pricing | 6. Save | Choosing a model | Recommended settings | Keeping your key safe | Troubleshooting
content: AI Setup (OpenRouter) RJ Nexus uses OpenRouter to power its advanced AI features: Auto SEO: generates and audits SEO titles and descriptions. AI Translation: translates content while preserving HTML. AI Code Review: checks theme and plugin files for bugs and security risks. OpenRouter gives you access to hundreds of AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and more) through a single API key, so you can switch models at any time without changing anything else. Video Guide: Prefer a video walkthrough? Watch the OpenRouter Setup Tutorial on YouTube. Time needed: about 5 minutes. What you need An email address or a Google/GitHub account to sign up at OpenRouter. Access to your RJ Nexus admin panel (an Admin account). (Optional) A small credit balance on OpenRouter if you want to use paid models. Free models (their names end with :free) cost nothing, but they have usage limits. Contents Part 1: Creating an OpenRouter API key Part 2: Configuring RJ Nexus Choosing a model Recommended settings Keeping your key safe Troubleshooting --- Part 1: Creating an OpenRouter API Key 1. Create an account Go to openrouter.ai and click Sign Up or Sign In in the top right corner. 2. Open the Keys page Once logged in, you will see the dashboard. In the sidebar, click Keys (highlighted in red). 3. Create a new key On the Keys screen, click the New Key button. 4. Configure the key A window will appear where you can set: | Field | What it does | Suggestion | |-------|--------------|------------| | Name | A label for the key | RJ Nexus Site | | Expiration | When the key stops working | Leave empty, or set a date if you rotate keys regularly | | Credit limit | Maximum spending for this key | Set a small limit (for example $5) to avoid surprise bills | 5. Copy your API key Once created, your API key is shown on screen. Copy it immediately and store it somewhere safe, such as a password manager. OpenRouter will not show it again. (Optional) You can manage your keys later by clicking them in the list. There you can view each key's configuration, limits and usage. --- Part 2: Configuring RJ Nexus 1. Open the AI settings In the admin sidebar, open Settings. In the settings grid, click the AI card. 2. Paste your API key Paste the key you copied from OpenRouter into the API Key field. 3. Understand the AI settings screen This is the main AI configuration screen. Each colored box marks one section: | Box | Section | What it does | |-----|---------|--------------| | Red | API Endpoint | The default OpenRouter URL. Do not change it unless OpenRouter changes its API address. | | Green | Default Model | The AI model used by all features. Type a model name manually or use the Fetch button. | | Yellow | AI Parameters | Controls how the AI behaves (see below). | | Blue | Save | Saves your configuration. | AI Parameters Temperature: lower values (for example 0.2) make answers focused and predictable, higher values (for example 0.8) make them more creative. Max Tokens: the maximum length of the AI's response. Timeout: how long to wait for a response before giving up. 4. Fetch and select a model To load the list of available models, click Fetch next to the Default Model field. A dropdown list appears. Search for the model you want and select it (for example google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free). 5. Check model pricing To see what a model costs, click the Get API Key button (or the link next to the model list) to open the OpenRouter models page. The model list shows pricing for each model: Example: If a model says $3/M input tokens and $15/M output tokens, you pay $3 for every 1 million tokens you send to the AI and $15 for every 1 million tokens it generates. Free models show $0. 6. Save After pasting the key and selecting a model, click Save Changes at the bottom of the page. The AI features are now active. --- Choosing a model There is no single best model. Pick based on what you need: | Goal | What to look for | |------|------------------| | Trying things out | A :free model. Zero cost, but slower and rate limited. | | Everyday SEO and writing | A fast, low-cost model. Cheaper models are usually good enough. | | Translation | A model that is strong in your target languages. Test with a short text first. | | Code review | A larger model. It must return valid JSON, and weaker models sometimes do not. | Tip: start with a free or cheap model, check the results, and upgrade only if the quality is not good enough. Recommended settings These are starting points, not strict rules. Adjust them to your results. | Setting | Suggested value | Notes | |---------|-----------------|-------| | Temperature | 0.2 to 0.4 | Best for SEO, translation and code review, where accuracy matters. Raise it for creative writing. | | Max Tokens | 1500 or higher | Increase it if long answers or translations are cut off. | | Timeout | 60 seconds or more | Large models and long texts can take a while to respond. | Keeping your key safe Your API key lets anyone spend your OpenRouter credits, so treat it like a password. Never share it in screenshots, chats, videos or public repositories. Set a credit limit on the key when you create it. Use a separate key for each website so you can disable one without affecting the others. If a key leaks, delete it on the OpenRouter Keys page and create a new one, then paste the new key in Settings → AI. Troubleshooting | Problem | Likely cause | What to do | |---------|--------------|------------| | "Invalid API key" or authentication error | Key copied incorrectly, or it was deleted or expired | Create a new key and paste it again. Make sure there are no spaces before or after it. | | "Insufficient credits" or payment error | A paid model is selected and your balance is empty | Add credits on OpenRouter, or switch to a :free model. | | Rate limit error (429) | Free models have strict usage limits | Wait a minute and retry, or choose another model. | | Model not found | The model was renamed or removed by its provider | Click Fetch and select a model from the current list. | | Request times out | The model is slow or busy, or the text is long | Increase Timeout, shorten the text, or pick a faster model. | | Fetch button shows no models | Key is missing or invalid, or the server cannot reach OpenRouter | Check the key first. If it is correct, make sure your hosting allows outgoing requests to openrouter.ai. | | AI Code Review says it could not parse the response | The model did not return valid JSON | Choose a stronger model and try again. | | Answers are cut off | Max Tokens is too low | Increase Max Tokens. | Still stuck? Ask in GitHub Discussions and include the error message (never your API key).

title: Auto SEO (Posts & Pages)
headings: Auto SEO (Posts & Pages) | Before you start | Step 1: Open the Edit Screen | Step 2: Go to the SEO Tab | Step 3: Run Auto SEO | Review the result | Step 4: Save Before You Analyze | Step 5: Analyze Your SEO | Understanding your score | What the messages mean | Why is my score low? (for example 30/100) | How to reach a high score | Troubleshooting | Good to know
content: Auto SEO (Posts & Pages) RJ Nexus includes a built-in AI-powered SEO assistant that helps your content rank better in search engines. With one click it reads your content and writes the SEO metadata for you: SEO Title: the headline shown in search results. SEO Description: the short summary shown under the title. Focus Keyword: the main phrase your page should rank for. Posts and Pages share the exact same SEO logic, so everything in this guide applies to both. Video Guide: Prefer a video walkthrough? Watch the Auto SEO Tutorial on YouTube. --- Before you start Make sure these three things are ready, otherwise Auto SEO will not give good results: AI is configured. Auto SEO uses the AI connection from Settings → AI. If you have not set it up yet, follow the AI Setup (OpenRouter) guide first. Your page has real content. The AI works only with the text on your page. The more useful text you write, the better the SEO data it can produce. You know where Save is. The Save button is at the top right of the edit screen. You will use it in Step 4. --- Step 1: Open the Edit Screen Go to Posts (or Pages) in the admin sidebar. Find the item you want to optimize and click the Edit button. --- Step 2: Go to the SEO Tab On the edit screen, find the tabs at the top of the content area and click SEO. --- Step 3: Run Auto SEO Inside the SEO section, click the Auto SEO button. Please wait. The AI reads all the content on your page to generate the most relevant SEO data. This can take a few moments. Do not close or refresh the page while the loading animation is active. When it finishes, the AI fills in the SEO Title, SEO Description and Focus Keyword fields automatically, based on your content. Tip: If you already wrote your own SEO fields, copy them somewhere safe before running Auto SEO, because the AI can replace what is in those fields. Review the result The AI gives you a strong starting point, but you know your content best. Take a minute to read each field and adjust it if needed: SEO Title: should describe the page clearly and contain your main keyword, ideally close to the beginning. SEO Description: should read like a short, natural invitation to click, not a list of keywords. Focus Keyword: should be the exact phrase people would type into a search engine to find this page. --- Step 4: Save Before You Analyze This step is the one most people skip, and it is the most common reason for a strange score. The Analyze feature checks the saved data in the database, not the temporary text you see in your browser. If you ran Auto SEO but have not saved yet, the analyzer is still looking at the old, empty fields and will show a very low score. Always click Save at the top right of the screen first. Then run Analyze. --- Step 5: Analyze Your SEO After saving, click the Analyze button to check how well the page is optimized. The system checks your page against standard SEO rules and shows a score out of 100, with a list of things to fix. --- Understanding your score What the messages mean Here are the messages you may see and how to fix each one: "SEO title is too short (11 chars, aim for 50-60)." Your title is too short to describe the page. Expand it so it explains what the page is about, and aim for 50 to 60 characters. "SEO description is too short (48 chars, aim for 150-160)." The description has room for more detail. Write one or two complete sentences that summarize the page and aim for 150 to 160 characters. "Focus keyword is not set." Enter the main phrase you want to rank for, or run Auto SEO again after saving your content. "Content is very short (67 words, aim for 300+)." The page does not have enough text. Add more useful information until the page reaches at least 300 words. Why is my score low? (for example 30/100) A low score usually has one of two causes: The page content is too short. Even though the AI generated the SEO data, it can only work with the text you provide. If your post or page has very little text, the AI cannot invent a 300+ word article. It creates the best possible metadata for the short content it has, and the analyzer will still flag the short content. The page was not saved. If you did not click Save after running Auto SEO, the analyzer reads the old empty data. See Step 4. --- How to reach a high score Follow this checklist for the best results: Write at least 300 words of helpful, original content. Choose one clear focus keyword and use it naturally in the title, the description and the text. Keep the SEO title between 50 and 60 characters. Keep the SEO description between 150 and 160 characters. Run Auto SEO, review the result, then click Save. Click Analyze and fix anything still listed. Save again after every change, then analyze again. --- Troubleshooting Nothing happens when I click Auto SEO. The AI may not be configured. Open Settings → AI and check that your API key and model are saved. See AI Setup (OpenRouter). I see an error message after clicking Auto SEO. Common causes are an invalid API key, an empty credit balance on a paid model, or a busy free model. Try again after a minute, or choose another model in Settings → AI. The fields stay empty or the result looks wrong. The page may have too little text. Add more content, save, and run Auto SEO again. The score is still low after I fixed everything. Confirm that you clicked Save before clicking Analyze. The analyzer only sees saved data. The loading takes very long. Long pages and large models take more time. Wait for the animation to finish. If it never finishes, reload the page and try again, or switch to a faster model. --- Good to know Auto SEO is an assistant, not a replacement for good content. The best SEO result always comes from helpful, original text combined with accurate metadata. You can run Auto SEO as many times as you like. Each run uses your configured AI model, so a paid model uses a small amount of your OpenRouter credit. Posts and Pages work identically, so you can use the same steps for both.

title: 🎨 Developer: Custom Color Presets
headings: 🎨 Developer: Custom Color Presets | 📑 On this page | 📍 Where presets live | 🧩 Preset structure | What each key controls | 🔢 Color format | 🚀 Step by step | 1️⃣ Open the helper file | 2️⃣ Add your preset | 3️⃣ Clear opcache | 4️⃣ Select your preset | 🎁 Ready-to-use presets | ⚡ Set a preset from code | ⚠️ Updates will overwrite core files | 🛠️ Troubleshooting | 🔗 Related
content: 🎨 Developer: Custom Color Presets Level File Time ✨ In one sentence: add one array entry to rjcolorpresets(), reload PHP, and your own admin color theme shows up in Settings → Colors. Only want to change colors from the admin panel, with no code? Read the Colors guide instead. --- 📑 On this page Where presets live Preset structure Color format Step by step Ready-to-use presets Set a preset from code Updates will overwrite core files Troubleshooting --- 📍 Where presets live Every color preset is defined in one place: app/Helpers/rj.php → rjcolorpresets() Each key of the returned array is a preset ID. Each value is an array with a label and six RGB colors. --- 🧩 Preset structure 'my-preset' => [ 'label' => 'My Preset', 'purple' => 'R G B', 'purple-light' => 'R G B', 'pink' => 'R G B', 'dark-1' => 'R G B', 'dark-2' => 'R G B', 'dark-3' => 'R G B', ], ### What each key controls | | Key | CSS variable | Where it shows | |:-:|-----|--------------|----------------| | 🟣 | purple | --rj-purple | Primary buttons, active nav items, links | | 💜 | purple-light | --rj-purple-light | Hover states, lighter accents | | 🌸 | pink | --rj-pink | Secondary accent, gradient end | | ⚫ | dark-1 | --rj-dark-1 | Main dark background | | 🌑 | dark-2 | --rj-dark-2 | Slightly lighter surface | | 🌒 | dark-3 | --rj-dark-3 | Card / panel surface | 🏷️ The label is the name shown in the picker. The array key (for example my-preset) is what gets stored in the admincolorpreset option. 📝 The key names say purple and pink for historical reasons. They simply mean primary, primary (light) and secondary accent, whatever the real color is. --- 🔢 Color format Colors are space-separated RGB integers (0–255). Not hex, not comma-separated, not rgb(). // ✅ Correct 'purple' => '124 58 237', // ❌ Wrong, will not render 'purple' => '#7c3aed', 'purple' => '124,58,237', 'purple' => 'rgb(124,58,237)', Hex → RGB by hand: split the hex into pairs and convert each one. #7c3aed → 7c=124, 3a=58, ed=237 → 124 58 237. Hex → RGB with PHP: paste this anywhere (a tinker session works too): [$r, $g, $b] = sscanf('#7c3aed', '#%02x%02x%02x'); echo "$r $g $b"; // 124 58 237 > 💡 Tip: keep dark-1 [ / ... / ], // ... existing presets 'ember' => [ 'label' => 'Ember', 'purple' => '232 73 29', 'purple-light' => '255 138 91', 'pink' => '13 148 136', 'dark-1' => '20 20 22', 'dark-2' => '33 33 36', 'dark-3' => '48 48 52', ], ]; ### 3️⃣ Clear opcache If PHP opcache is enabled, reload PHP-FPM (or clear opcache) so the new code is loaded. | Hosting | What to do | |---------|------------| | Shared hosting | Saving the file is usually enough | | VPS | systemctl reload php8.2-fpm (adjust the version) | 4️⃣ Select your preset Open the admin panel → Settings → Colors. Your new preset now appears as a selectable card. Settings → Colors: every preset is a card with a live color preview. Select it and save. Admin colors update immediately. 🎉 --- 🎁 Ready-to-use presets Four presets that look nothing like the built-in ones. Each uses a hue range and a background family that the others do not, so they are easy to tell apart in the picker. Copy any of them into rjcolorpresets(). | Preset | Idea | Primary | Light | Accent | Backgrounds | |--------|------|:-------:|:-----:|:------:|:-----------:| | Ember 🔥 | Vermilion on neutral charcoal, teal accent | #E8491D | #FF8A5B | #0D9488 | | | Lime 🍋 | Acid lime on olive-black, citrus accent | #65A30D | #BEF264 | #FACC15 | | | Fuchsia 💖 | Neon magenta on plum-black, electric cyan accent | #C026D3 | #E879F9 | #22D3EE | | | Mono 🩶 | Silver on pure neutral black, no hue at all | #71717A | #D4D4D8 | #F4F4F5 | | 📋 Copy the PHP for all four 'ember' => [ 'label' => 'Ember', 'purple' => '232 73 29', 'purple-light' => '255 138 91', 'pink' => '13 148 136', 'dark-1' => '20 20 22', 'dark-2' => '33 33 36', 'dark-3' => '48 48 52', ], 'lime' => [ 'label' => 'Lime', 'purple' => '101 163 13', 'purple-light' => '190 242 100', 'pink' => '250 204 21', 'dark-1' => '14 18 6', 'dark-2' => '26 33 10', 'dark-3' => '38 48 15', ], 'fuchsia' => [ 'label' => 'Fuchsia', 'purple' => '192 38 211', 'purple-light' => '232 121 249', 'pink' => '34 211 238', 'dark-1' => '24 6 30', 'dark-2' => '40 10 52', 'dark-3' => '58 14 74', ], 'mono' => [ 'label' => 'Mono', 'purple' => '113 113 122', 'purple-light' => '212 212 216', 'pink' => '244 244 245', 'dark-1' => '10 10 12', 'dark-2' => '24 24 27', 'dark-3' => '39 39 42', ], --- ⚡ Set a preset from code To activate a preset without touching the UI: rjsetoption('admincolorpreset', 'ember'); rjflushoptions(); The admin panel uses the new colors on the next request. --- ⚠️ Updates will overwrite core files app/Helpers/rj.php is part of the core. When you update RJ Nexus this file is replaced, and your custom preset will be lost. | Option | How | |--------|-----| | 📎 Keep a snippet | Store your preset code outside the project and re-add it after each update | | 🌿 Use a branch | Keep your edits in a fork or a private branch | | 🤝 Send a pull request | If the preset is useful to everyone, submit it to rj-nexus/rj-nexus so it ships in the next release | 💡 rj-content/themes/ and rj-content/plugins/ are never touched by core updates. A small plugin or a theme README is a safe place to keep your preset snippet. --- 🛠️ Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | Preset does not appear in Settings → Colors | Old code is cached by opcache | Reload PHP-FPM or clear opcache | | Colors look broken or unchanged | A color is not in R G B format | Use space-separated integers, never hex or rgb() | | Admin falls back to purple | The saved preset ID no longer exists | Pick a preset again in Settings → Colors or call rjsetoption() with a valid ID | | Preset vanished after an update | rj.php was replaced by the new version | Re-add your entry (see the section above) | | Text is hard to read on buttons | purple is too light for white text | Use a darker primary and keep the light shade in purple-light` | --- 🔗 Related 📘 Colors: end-user guide for changing admin, frontend and theme colors from the UI

title: Colors
headings: Colors | 1. Admin Panel Colors | 2. Frontend Site Colors | 3. Theme Colors | Which one should I use?
content: Colors RJ Nexus lets you change colors in three separate places, each controlling a different part of the system. Pick the one that matches what you want to change. | What you want to change | Where to go | |---|---| | Admin panel look (sidebar, buttons, links) | Settings → Colors | | Frontend site colors (visitors see these) | Appearance → Colors | | Theme-specific colors (if the active theme supports them) | Appearance → Customize | --- 1. Admin Panel Colors These colors control the appearance of the admin panel itself - the sidebar, primary buttons, links, and gradient accents. They do not affect the frontend. Step 1 — From the sidebar open Settings, then locate the Colors card in the settings grid. Step 2 — Choose a preset or adjust individual colors. Changes apply to the admin panel immediately after saving. --- 2. Frontend Site Colors These colors are the ones visitors see on your public site - links, buttons, and global accent colors shared by every theme. Step 1 — From the sidebar open Appearance, then click Colors. Step 2 — Select a global color preset or fine-tune the individual values. These act as the base palette for the frontend. --- 3. Theme Colors Some themes provide their own dedicated color controls, independent of the global frontend colors above. If your active theme supports customization, you can override its colors from the theme customizer. These settings apply only to the active theme. Step 1 — From the sidebar open Appearance, then click Customize for the active theme. Step 2 — Open the Colors section of the customizer and adjust the theme-specific values. Each control maps directly to a CSS variable used by the theme. --- Which one should I use? To rebrand the admin panel, use Settings → Colors. To change the frontend base palette across all themes, use Appearance → Colors. To tweak colors for the currently active theme only, use Appearance → Customize (only if the theme exposes color controls). If both Appearance → Colors and the theme customizer are set, the theme customizer values win — they are more specific.

title: Installation Guide
headings: Installation Guide | Requirements | Step 1: Download the ZIP | Step 2: Upload to Your Server | Step 3: Run the Installer
content: Installation Guide This guide will walk you through the process of installing RJ Nexus CMS on your server. RJ Nexus is designed to be lightweight and can be installed on almost any shared hosting or VPS without requiring SSH access or complex terminal commands. Requirements Before you begin, ensure your server meets the following minimum requirements: PHP >= 8.2 Database: MySQL 5.7+ or MariaDB 10.3+ Web Server: Apache or Nginx PHP Extensions: PDO, mbstring, openssl, fileinfo, gd, zip, curl, json, tokenizer, xml, ctype Note: RJ Nexus no longer requires the exec() or proc_open() functions to be enabled. This makes it fully compatible with highly restrictive shared hosting environments. You do not need to ask your hosting provider to change PHP settings. Step 1: Download the ZIP Go to the RJ Nexus GitHub Releases page. Download the latest .zip file for the stable release. Step 2: Upload to Your Server Log in to your hosting control panel (cPanel, Plesk, or your VPS file manager). Navigate to your website's root directory (usually public_html or www). Upload the .zip file you downloaded. Extract the ZIP file directly in the public_html folder. Make sure the extracted files are in the root folder, not inside another subfolder. Step 3: Run the Installer Open your web browser and navigate to your domain:

title: Manual Update
headings: Manual Update | Before You Start | Step 1: Download the Latest Version | Option A: GitHub | Option B: Official Website | Update on Hostinger (hPanel) | Step 1: Open File Manager | Step 2: Upload the ZIP File | Step 3: Extract the ZIP | Step 4: Replace Existing Files | Update on cPanel | After the Update | Troubleshooting | Need Hosting?
content: Manual Update This guide shows how to update RJ Nexus manually, without any command line. It covers Hostinger (hPanel) and cPanel. The process is the same on both: download the new version, upload it, extract it over the old files, and keep two protected files untouched. 🎥 Prefer video? Watch the full walkthrough: Manual Update on YouTube --- Before You Start Create a backup of your site files and database (hosting panel → Backups). Make sure you know where your site lives. On most hosts it is the public_html folder. Read the warning below. It is the most important part of this guide. ⛔ DO NOT DELETE THESE FILES Your site will break or ask for a fresh installation if either of them is lost. | File | Location | Why it matters | |------|----------|----------------| | .env | public_html/.env | Holds your database connection, app key and all settings | | Installed lock file | inside public_html/public/ | Tells the system it is already installed, so the installer does not run again | Never delete, rename or replace them. If you remove old files before extracting, skip these two. .env location: .env file, do not delete Installed lock file location: Installed lock file, do not delete --- Step 1: Download the Latest Version Choose one of the two sources. Option A: GitHub Open the releases page: Find the latest release and download the source/package .zip file. Download from GitHub Option B: Official Website Open the official website: Click the Download button in the header. On the Download page, pick the latest version and download the ZIP file. Keep the downloaded .zip file. Do not extract it on your computer. --- Update on Hostinger (hPanel) Step 1: Open File Manager Log in to hPanel, select your website, and open File Manager. Open File Manager Then open the public_html folder, where your site files are. public_html folder Remember: do not delete .env or the installed lock file. Step 2: Upload the ZIP File Click the Upload button and select the .zip file you downloaded. Wait until the upload reaches 100%. Upload ZIP Step 3: Extract the ZIP Right-click the uploaded .zip file and choose Extract. Extract it into public_html so the new files overwrite the old ones. Extract ZIP Step 4: Replace Existing Files If the File Manager asks about existing files, choose Replace / Overwrite, so the old files are updated with the new version. Replace files After the extraction finishes, delete the uploaded .zip file to keep your hosting clean. --- Update on cPanel The idea is exactly the same as on Hostinger. Only the interface looks different. Log in to cPanel and open File Manager (under Files). Go to the folder where your site is installed, usually public_html. Click Upload at the top, then drag and drop the .zip file. Wait for it to finish, then click Go Back. Reload the folder (the Reload button) so the .zip file appears in the list. Right-click the .zip file and choose Extract. Make sure the extraction path is /public_html (or your site's folder), then click Extract File(s). cPanel overwrites files with the same name automatically. Your .env and installed lock file are not part of the package, so they stay untouched, but never delete them by hand. When extraction is done, delete the .zip file. Tip: If the new files extracted into an extra subfolder (for example rj-nexus-1.2.3/), open that folder, select all files, and Move them into public_html, choosing to overwrite. Then delete the empty folder. --- After the Update Open your website and the admin panel to confirm everything loads. Clear your site cache (from the admin panel if available) and your browser cache (Ctrl + F5). Check the version number in the admin panel to confirm the update was applied. Troubleshooting | Problem | Solution | |---------|----------| | Installer screen appears again | The installed lock file was deleted. Restore it from your backup. | | Database / 500 error after update | The .env file was removed or replaced. Restore it from your backup. | | Old design still visible | Clear site cache and browser cache. | | Files not overwritten | Extract again and choose Replace / Overwrite. | --- Need Hosting? RJ Nexus is an open-source project. If you are looking for reliable hosting, you can get 20% off Hostinger with our referral link. It also helps support the project at no extra cost to you: 👉 Get Hostinger with 20% discount

title: Plugin Development
headings: Plugin Development | What You Will Learn | Prerequisites | How Plugins Work | Plugin Directory Structure | Naming Rules | Step 1: Create the Metadata File | Field Reference | Step 2: Create the Service Provider | Step 3: Define Routes | Step 4: Create the Controller | Step 5: Create the View (Blade) | Step 6: Activate the Plugin | Going Further | Add a Database Table (Migrations) | Add a Model | Add Styles and Scripts | Add Translations | Use Hooks (Filters and Actions) | Protect Your Routes | Debugging and Troubleshooting | Best Practices | Packaging and Publishing | Plugin Checklist | Next Steps
content: Plugin Development RJ Nexus features a fully isolated, modular architecture. You can extend the CMS by creating your own plugins without modifying the core codebase. Each plugin brings its own routes, views, migrations, and assets, so it can be installed, updated, or removed without touching anything else. This guide walks you through building a basic "Hello World" plugin, then shows how to add a database, assets, translations, and hooks. What You Will Learn How a plugin is structured and discovered How to write plugin.json, a service provider, routes, a controller, and a view How to activate and debug your plugin How to extend it with migrations, assets, translations, and hooks How to package and publish it Prerequisites A working RJ Nexus installation (see the Installation Guide) PHP 8.2+ and basic knowledge of Laravel (service providers, routes, controllers, Blade) Access to the rj-content/plugins/ folder through FTP, File Manager, or your code editor Tip: RJ Nexus includes a built-in Plugin IDE with a code editor and AI code review, so you can write and review plugin code right inside the admin panel. --- How Plugins Work When the CMS boots, it scans rj-content/plugins/ for folders that contain a plugin.json file. For every active plugin, RJ Nexus registers the plugin's autoloader (using the namespace value) and runs its service provider. The provider then loads the plugin's routes, views, and any hooks. plugin.json → Autoloader → Service Provider → Routes / Views / Hooks Because the core is never modified, a broken or removed plugin cannot damage your site's core files. --- Plugin Directory Structure All plugins must be placed in the following directory: rj-content/plugins/ Each plugin has its own folder, named after its slug. A typical structure looks like this: rj-content/plugins/ └── my-awesome-plugin/ ├── plugin.json # Plugin metadata (name, author, version) ├── src/ │ ├── MyPluginServiceProvider.php # Entry point of the plugin │ └── Http/Controllers/ │ └── MyPluginController.php ├── routes/ │ └── web.php # Plugin routes └── views/ └── index.blade.php # Plugin views (UI) ### Naming Rules | Item | Rule | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | Folder / slug | Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only | my-awesome-plugin | | Namespace | PascalCase, no spaces or hyphens | MyAwesomePlugin | | View namespace | Same as the slug | my-awesome-plugin::index | | Route names | Prefixed with the slug | my-awesome-plugin.index | Important: The folder name, the slug in plugin.json, and the view namespace should all match. A mismatch is the most common reason a plugin does not load. --- Step 1: Create the Metadata File Every plugin requires a plugin.json file. It tells RJ Nexus that the folder is a plugin and provides its essential details. Create plugin.json inside your plugin folder: { "name": "My Awesome Plugin", "slug": "my-awesome-plugin", "version": "1.0.0", "author": "Your Name", "description": "A simple plugin that says hello.", "namespace": "MyAwesomePlugin", "provider": "MyAwesomePlugin\\MyPluginServiceProvider" } ### Field Reference | Field | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | name | Yes | The display name shown in Plugins → Manage | | slug | Yes | Unique identifier. Must match the folder name | | version | Yes | Version number using semantic versioning (1.0.0) | | author | Yes | Your name or company | | description | Yes | A short sentence describing what the plugin does | | namespace | Yes | Root PHP namespace that maps to the src/ folder | | provider | Yes | Fully qualified class name of the service provider | Note: In JSON, the backslash must be escaped, so write \\ between namespace parts. --- Step 2: Create the Service Provider The Service Provider is the entry point of your plugin. It loads your views and routes and registers any hooks. Create src/MyPluginServiceProvider.php: loadViewsFrom(DIR . '/../views', 'my-awesome-plugin'); // Register routes $this->loadRoutesFrom(DIR . '/../routes/web.php'); // You can also add hooks here using rjaddfilter or rjaddaction } } register() vs boot(): use register() only to bind things into the container. Use boot() for everything that depends on other services, such as views, routes, and hooks. --- Step 3: Define Routes Create routes/web.php to define where your plugin's pages will be accessible. name('my-awesome-plugin.index'); Always give your routes a name and prefix it with your plugin slug. This prevents clashes with other plugins and lets you generate links safely: route('my-awesome-plugin.index'); --- Step 4: Create the Controller Create src/Http/Controllers/MyPluginController.php: My Awesome Plugin {{ $message }} The admin panel uses Tailwind CSS, so you can style your page with the same utility classes used in the rest of the dashboard. --- Step 6: Activate the Plugin Log in to your RJ Nexus Admin Panel. Go to Plugins → Manage. You will see My Awesome Plugin in the list. Click Activate. Once activated, the plugin's Service Provider runs, its routes are registered, and you can open your new plugin page. Tip: If you make changes to your plugin's routes or service providers during development, you may need to run php artisan optimize:clear to see the changes immediately. --- Going Further The steps above give you a working plugin. The sections below show how to build something real. Add a Database Table (Migrations) Plugins can ship their own migrations. Create a database/migrations folder inside your plugin: my-awesome-plugin/ └── database/ └── migrations/ └── 20260101000000creategreetingstable.php id(); $table->string('message'); $table->timestamps(); }); } public function down(): void { Schema::dropIfExists('myplugin_greetings'); } }; Register the migrations in your service provider's boot() method: $this->loadMigrationsFrom(DIR . '/../database/migrations'); Then run them: php artisan migrate > Best practice: Always prefix your table names (for example myplugin_) so they never collide with core tables or other plugins. Implement down() properly so the table can be removed cleanly. Add a Model get(); ### Add Styles and Scripts Keep your plugin's assets inside the plugin folder: my-awesome-plugin/ └── assets/ ├── css/style.css └── js/app.js Publish them to a public location from your service provider: $this->publishes([ DIR . '/../assets' => public_path('plugins/my-awesome-plugin'), ], 'my-awesome-plugin-assets'); php artisan vendor:publish --tag=my-awesome-plugin-assets Then reference them in Blade: ### Add Translations RJ Nexus supports multiple languages, so make your plugin translatable from day one. my-awesome-plugin/ └── lang/ ├── en/messages.php └── az/messages.php // lang/en/messages.php return [ 'hello' => 'Hello from my awesome plugin!', ]; // In the service provider's boot() $this->loadTranslationsFrom(DIR . '/../lang', 'my-awesome-plugin'); {{ __('my-awesome-plugin::messages.hello') }} ### Use Hooks (Filters and Actions) Hooks let your plugin change or react to core behavior without editing core files. Register them in the service provider's boot() method using rjaddfilter and rjaddaction. | Hook type | Function | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | Action | rjaddaction | Run your code when something happens | | Filter | rjaddfilter | Receive a value, modify it, and return it | public function boot(): void { // ...views and routes... // A filter must always return the (modified) value rjaddfilter('examplehookname', function ($value) { return $value . ' (modified by my plugin)'; }); // An action just runs your code rjaddaction('exampleeventname', function () { // do something }); } > Note: examplehookname and exampleeventname are placeholders. Check the list of available hooks in the core code or in the Plugin IDE for the real names. Protect Your Routes Plugin pages in the admin area should only be visible to authorized users. Wrap your routes in the appropriate middleware: Route::middleware(['web', 'auth'])->group(function () { Route::get('/my-awesome-plugin', [MyPluginController::class, 'index']) ->name('my-awesome-plugin.index'); }); Always validate user input in your controllers: $validated = $request->validate([ 'message' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'], ]); --- Debugging and Troubleshooting | Problem | Likely cause | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | | Plugin does not appear in Plugins → Manage | Missing or invalid plugin.json | Check the file name, valid JSON syntax (no trailing commas), and the folder location | | "Class not found" error | Namespace does not match the folder structure | Make sure namespace in plugin.json matches the PHP namespace and that files live under src/ | | View [my-awesome-plugin::index] not found | View namespace mismatch | Use the same name in loadViewsFrom() and in view() | | Route returns 404 | Routes are cached or not loaded | Run php artisan optimize:clear and check php artisan route:list | | Changes are not visible | Cached views, config, or routes | Run php artisan optimize:clear | | White screen or HTTP 500 | PHP error in your code | Check storage/logs/laravel.log | | Plugin breaks the site after activation | Fatal error in the provider | Rename the plugin folder (for example add -disabled) via FTP to deactivate it, then fix the error | Useful commands during development: php artisan optimize:clear # clear all caches php artisan route:list # show every registered route php artisan migrate:status # show which migrations have run --- Best Practices Keep it isolated. Never edit core files. Use hooks, routes, and views to extend the CMS. Use a unique prefix for table names, route names, config keys, and CSS classes. Follow PSR-12 coding standards and use type hints. Validate and escape. Validate every input and use {{ }} (escaped output) in Blade. Use {!! !!} only for trusted HTML. Protect admin routes with authentication and permission checks. Make it translatable. Use translation keys instead of hard-coded text. Clean up after yourself. Provide down() methods in migrations. Version carefully. Follow semantic versioning and keep a changelog. Do not commit secrets. Keep API keys and passwords out of your code and repository. --- Packaging and Publishing When your plugin is ready: Update the version in plugin.json (for example 1.0.0 → 1.1.0). Test activation, deactivation, and a fresh install on a clean site. Create a ZIP of the plugin folder, with plugin.json at the top level of the plugin folder. Publish it on GitHub. RJ Nexus delivers plugin updates through GitHub, so tag a release for each new version. git tag v1.1.0 git push origin v1.1.0 Users can then install your plugin by placing it in rj-content/plugins/ and activating it under Plugins → Manage. --- Plugin Checklist Before you release, confirm that: [ ] plugin.json is valid and every required field is filled in [ ] The folder name, slug, and view namespace match [ ] The plugin activates and deactivates without errors [ ] Routes are named, prefixed, and protected [ ] Inputs are validated and output is escaped [ ] Migrations run cleanly and have a working down() [ ] Text is translatable [ ] A README explains installation and usage --- Next Steps Study the Form Builder plugin as a real-world example of a larger plugin Learn how themes and RJBuilder widgets work Use the built-in Plugin IDE for editing and AI code review Report bugs or request features on the GitHub issue tracker

title: RJ Builder
headings: RJ Builder | Why RJ Builder? | 🌍 Multilingual by design | Everything else you expect from a modern builder | Getting Started | The Editor at a Glance | Settings tabs (right panel) | Working with Drag & Drop | Editing in Multiple Languages | Responsive Design | Dynamic Tags | Global Widgets and Templates | AI Assistant | For Developers: Core Structure | Documentation and Updates | License
content: RJ Builder RJ Builder is the visual page builder built into RJ Nexus. If you have used Elementor or the BeTheme (Muffin) Builder, you already know how it works: you drag elements onto a canvas, edit them in place, style them from a side panel, and see the result instantly. No code required. You can build full pages, headers, footers, popups and reusable blocks, all from one editor. --- Why RJ Builder? 🌍 Multilingual by design This is the biggest advantage of RJ Builder. Every page you build can be edited in several languages at the same time, directly inside the builder. Switch between languages in the editor without leaving the page. Translate each text, button, image and link for every language. Keep one layout and one design. Only the content changes per language. Publish all languages together with a single Save. In many other systems (for example WordPress) multilingual editing requires extra plugins, duplicated pages or separate translation workflows. In RJ Nexus it is part of the core builder. Everything else you expect from a modern builder | Feature | What it does | |---------|--------------| | Drag & Drop | Add, move and rearrange elements visually on the canvas | | Live Editing | Click any text or element and edit it right on the page | | Responsive Controls | Set spacing, typography and visibility separately for Desktop, Tablet and Mobile | | Dynamic Tags | Bind live data (site title, user info, post data) to any text or image field | | Global Widgets | Save a section once and reuse it across many pages. Edit it once, update it everywhere | | Template Library | Create, export and import reusable sections and full templates | | AI Assistant | Generate text, improve your copy and get layout suggestions | | Dark Mode Editor | A clean, distraction-free interface | --- Getting Started Open your admin panel and go to RJ Builder (/admin/rjbuilder). Create a new template. Choose the type: Page, Header, Footer, Popup or Block. Use the Add Element panel on the left to insert widgets onto the canvas. Click any element and customize it from the right panel (see below). Click Save to publish your changes. --- The Editor at a Glance | Area | Purpose | |------|---------| | Left panel | Add Element: all available widgets, ready to drag onto the canvas | | Canvas (center) | Your live page. Drag, drop, reorder and edit directly | | Right panel | Settings of the selected element | | Top bar | Language switcher, device preview (Desktop / Tablet / Mobile), Save | Settings tabs (right panel) Content: texts, images, links, icons, repeater items and dynamic tags. Style: colors, typography, spacing, borders, shadows and backgrounds. Motion: entrance effects and animations. --- Working with Drag & Drop Find a widget in the Add Element panel. Drag it onto the canvas and drop it where you want it. Drag the element again to move it, or drop it into another section or column. Select an element to edit its content and style. Complex layouts are built the same way: add a section, place columns inside it, and fill the columns with widgets. --- Editing in Multiple Languages Open any template in RJ Builder. Choose the language from the language switcher. Edit the texts, buttons, images and links for that language. Switch to the next language and repeat. Click Save. All languages are saved together. Tip: Build the design once in your main language first. Then switch to the other languages and only translate the content. The layout, spacing and styles stay identical everywhere. The languages available on your site's frontend are managed from the admin panel's language settings. --- Responsive Design Every element can look different on each device. Switch the preview to Desktop, Tablet or Mobile. Change spacing, font sizes and alignment for that device only. Hide or show elements on specific devices. Changes made on a smaller device do not affect the larger ones. --- Dynamic Tags Dynamic tags let you connect a field to live data instead of typing a fixed value. Use them for things like: Site title User information Post data Click the dynamic tag icon next to a text or image field and choose the data source. --- Global Widgets and Templates Global Widgets: save any section as a global widget. When you edit it, every page using it updates automatically. Great for call-to-action bars, contact blocks and footers. Templates: save sections or complete pages as templates, then export them as a file and import them on another site. --- AI Assistant The built-in AI assistant helps you work faster: Generate text for a section Improve or rewrite existing copy Suggest layout sections for your page --- For Developers: Core Structure | Path | Description | |------|-------------| | edit.blade.php | Main editor interface (HTML structure) | | layout.blade.php | Base layout wrapper for the editor | | partials/ | UI partials: styles, field types (repeater, color, media, etc.) and core JavaScript logic | | widgets/builtin/ | Blade views of all core widgets | --- Documentation and Updates This page explains how RJ Builder works in general. For the full list of widgets, new features, improvements and bug fixes, see the CHANGELOG.md file in the project root. New widgets and improvements are documented only in the changelog, so this guide stays clean and stable. License RJ Builder is a proprietary component of RJ NEXUS.

headings: Languages & Translation | 1. Accessing Language Settings | 2. General Language Settings | 3. Managing Languages | Add a New Language | Select Frontend Languages | Edit Language Name | Change Language Flag | Delete a Language | 4. Using the Translation Editor | AI Translation Setup | The Translation Screen
content: Languages & Translation RJ Nexus allows you to manage multiple languages, change the admin and frontend locales, translate your content, and fully customize the translation strings. This guide covers everything from adding a new language to using the built-in translation editor. --- 1. Accessing Language Settings Step 1 — From the admin sidebar, navigate to Settings. Step 2 — In the settings grid, locate and click on the Language card. Step 3 — This opens the main Language management screen. --- 2. General Language Settings At the bottom of the Language screen, you will find the core configuration options. Admin Language: Sets the default language for your admin panel. Frontend Language: Sets the default fallback language for your public site. Auto-detect browser language: If enabled, the system automatically sets the locale based on the visitor's browser language. Enable RTL support: Automatically applies Right-to-Left layout direction for languages like Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Urdu. --- 3. Managing Languages Add a New Language You can add a new language to the system by clicking the Add Language button. Select Frontend Languages Choose which languages are visible to your visitors on the frontend. Only the selected languages will appear in the frontend language switcher. Edit Language Name You can rename the languages to fit your site's needs. Change Language Flag You can change the country flag associated with a language by uploading a new icon. Delete a Language System languages can be deleted using the trash icon next to the language. --- 4. Using the Translation Editor To translate the static strings (UI text) of your site, click the Translate button next to any language. AI Translation Setup At the bottom of the language settings, you will find the AI Translation option. Important: The Auto Translate feature requires an OpenRouter API key to function. If you haven't set it up yet, follow the AI Setup (OpenRouter) guide. The Translation Screen When you open the translation editor, you will see a detailed interface. Here is a breakdown of the 5 colored areas: Green Box (Auto Translate): Click this to automatically translate missing strings using AI. (Requires OpenRouter setup). Red Box (Search): Use this search bar to find specific keys or translations. You can search in any language to quickly locate and edit a string. Purple Box (Keys): These are the original strings or keys that need to be translated (usually in English). Yellow Box (Strings): This is where the actual translation goes. Edit the text here to change what the user sees. Blue Button (Save): Click this button to save all your changes to the translation files.
